issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5.2.4 ofType(type : type specifier)
issues.evidence: Spec says ofType() returns items of the given type or a subclass. Reproducer: Bundle.entry.resource.ofType(Resource).id and .ofType(DomainResource).id over Patient+Observation resources returned [] in both Python core and native/fallback DuckDB paths; expected Patient/Observation ids because both resources inherit from DomainResource and Resource.
issues.root_cause: Python core and native C++ ofType() used exact type identity for all inputs, so FHIR resource supertypes such as DomainResource and Resource were not considered. The initial broad subtype fix was narrowed after R4 conformance confirmed primitive ofType(string) must still reject FHIR code.
issues.resolution: Added generated FHIR parent hierarchy awareness to Python TypeInfo and C++ fn_isType/evalOfType, applying subtype matching for non-primitive FHIR types while preserving primitive exactness. Rebuilt and copied the bundled DuckDB extension.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5 function expression parameter rules and §5.2.3 repeat(projection)
issues.evidence: Spec says expression parameters are evaluated per input item and may refer to $this and $index. Python fallback leaves $index visible after where()/select() and does not bind it during repeat(). Reproducers: item.select(linkId) | $index returned ['a','b','1'] in fallback vs ['a','b'] native; item.repeat(iif($index = 0, item, {})).linkId returned [] fallback vs ['a1'] native.
issues.root_cause: Python macro implementations for where() and select() mutated the shared evaluation context without restoring $index, and repeat() never bound $index while evaluating each queued item.
issues.resolution: Wrapped where(), select(), and repeat() macro index binding in save/restore logic; repeat() now binds a monotonically increasing item index. Undefined $index/$total now evaluate to empty instead of raising, matching the wrapper contract and native behavior.
